text:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — enterprise customers are pushing hard for deterministic egress IPs for private deployments so they can whitelist traffic. We need a recommended launch approach, acceptance criteria, and upgrade path options. cc @Sam (Field) @Rory (NetOps)

Sam (Field): Yep, multiple customers (finance + healthcare) require static IPs. They also require minimal downtime during upgrades. Some use legacy firewalls that only accept single IP blocks.

Rory (NetOps): Two main patterns: 1) operator-managed NAT IPs (we provide stable egress IPs from our VPC) 2) customer-managed IPs (they provision and route traffic to us). Operator-managed is easiest UX but means we maintain public IPs and handle compliance. Customer-managed preserves tenant ownership but complicates support and diagnostics.

Luca (Eng): For operator-managed NAT we'd implement a pooled NAT instance per-region, plus per-tenant mapping. That implies changes: a) egress controller for k8s sidecar b) routing / SNAT table changes c) billing impact for elastic IPs. Rolling upgrades should be doable with drain+rebind but sticky mappings are tricky.

Priya (Support): Logs: customers want source IP visible in our request logs (and X-Forwarded-For preserved). We also need audit entries for IP assignment changes and an automated notification to customers when IPs rotate. KMS/HSM calls unaffected but call paths must be documented.

Maya (PM): Good. Proposed phased rollout: Phase 1 (pilot): operator-managed static IPs for a handful of customers, manual provisioning, clear rollback. Phase 2: automation + per-tenant pools + telemetry. Phase 3: support customer-managed IP handoff and migration automation. Need acceptance criteria for each phase.

Rory (NetOps): Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Pilot: stable egress IP per-tenant for 30d with no more than one unplanned rotation.
- Automation: API for provisioning/releasing IPs, telemetry shows <1s additional latency.
- Migration: documented procedures + automated migration tool that preserves IP mapping during rolling upgrades.

Luca (Eng): Implementation notes:
- Config: `egressPolicy: operator-managed | customer-managed` in tenant CR.
- Default: operator-managed for easier onboarding.
- Migration path: controller watches `egressPolicy` and orchestrates NAT reassignment.

Sam (Field): Field constraints:
- Some customers can't accept any external IPs owned by 3rd party. For those, we must support customer-owned IP lists.
- They also want a 'grace period' for DNS + firewall rule updates; recommend scheduled cutover windows.

Maya (PM): Prioritization ask: we have 3 paying customers who will convert to Dedicated if we support P1 operator static egress. Recommend marking pilot as P0 for Q2.

Luca (Eng): Rough estimate: pilot 2 devs * 6w, automation + telemetry 3 devs * 10w, migration tooling 2 devs * 8w. Need NetOps support for IP allocation and runbook.

Priya (Support): I'll draft support playbook + canned responses and add observability checklist (logs, alerts for IP rotations).

deploy-bot: infra-note: created ticket RW-ENG-5482 for `egress-ip-pilot` — link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-ENG-5482

Maya (PM): Action items: 1) Rory to own IP allocation runbook (due in 3d). 2) Luca to spike NAT controller and share prototype (EOD next Tue). 3) Sam to collect exact firewall rules from pilot customers. 4) Priya to draft support playbook. I'll add the pilot to the roadmap and ping legal for IP ownership language. If anyone wants to change prioritization, speak up here. :thumbsup:

Luca (Eng): +1 on spike. One question — do we want to explore a relay fallback (TLS relay through operator) for customers that block all outgoing except whitelisted IPs? That could be a lower-effort stopgap.

Rory (NetOps): Relay fallback is feasible but raises scale and cost concerns; we can include it as an off-ramp for pilot.

Maya (PM): OK — include relay fallback as optional P0' item for pilot. I'll create the roadmap ticket and assign owners. Thanks all.
